transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-01 15:00 PT | Duration: 52m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO, Cyclone Tech), Sofia Gomez (Sr. ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (Backend Lead), Priya Rao (Security)

Summary: Quick discovery oriented around using Redwood's self-serve/PLG API to get Cyclone's devs to first token quickly. Explore tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for their fraud detection agent. Next: provide credits, run a small benchmark (100k tokens/day simulation), and deep dive on security and VPC options.
Topics: quickstart flow, free credits, time-to-first-token, SDKs, rate limits, dedicated vs hosted, private/VPC, SOC2/KMS, latency vs cost, deployment timeline

00:00 - 00:32 Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ava from Redwood, i'll kick off, quick intros. we mostly want to understand your goals for the POC and how fast you want to get to first tokens.

00:33 - 01:10 Raj Patel: Hey thanks. i'm raj cto at cyclone. Our team's evaluating several options - we want a low friction way to let product experimenters run chat & classification models. main ask is speed to value and predictable cost for a pilot. also security constraints, obviously.
01:11 - 03:05 Daniel Park: Thanks raj. quick question - you said product experimenters, are they internal engineers or external? and what's your expected QPS and avg prompt length?

03:06 - 04:00 Sofia Gomez: Mostly internal engineers and a couple of beta partners. Expect peaks around 20-30 RPS for the pilot, avg prompt ~120 tokens, completions ~250 tokens. We're prototyping a fraud detection assistant that summarizes event context and suggests actions.

04:01 - 06:15 Ava Martinez: Great, that size is a perfect candidate for PLG quickstart. The fastest route is our hosted Redwood API - you sign up, redeem free credits, and you can hit first token in under 10 minutes using our SDKs. we also offer dedicated/reserved capacity and private deployments if you need isolation or SOC 2/contracting.
06:16 - 07:30 Liam O'Connor: When you say under 10 minutes - is that after signup or after security review? we need to know the steps for devs to start calling endpoints.

07:31 - 10:20 Maya Singh: Good question. In PLG flow: signup -> verify email -> create API key -> install SDK or call REST. for many teams first-token is literally within minutes once they have the key. separate enterprise onboarding (dedicated/private) involves contract and SSO setup which takes longer. you can start on Hosted and then migrate to Dedicated, we support pinning model versions so rollouts are seamless.

10:21 - 12:50 Priya Rao: From security side, what about data retention and encryption? our legal team will need SOC2 and KMS support, plus VPC connectivity for production. also need audit logs and RBAC.

12:51 - 15:30 Daniel Park: we do SOC 2 and can provide the security whitepaper. Hosted tenants get encrypted at rest and in transit; customers can opt for customer-managed keys (KMS) on Dedicated/Private. for VPC and private control plane that's our Private deployment - we can also run an on-prem package if needed. audit logs and per-token tracing are available in the Redwood Console.

15:31 - 18:05 Raj Patel: ok good. for the pilot we'll likely stay on Hosted due to speed, but we want the option to go to Dedicated within a quarter. any limits on bulk uploads or batch embeddings? also curious about caching - can we avoid repeated tokens costs?

18:06 - 21:40 Maya Singh: embeddings have batching and concurrency controls, and our Optimize tooling recommends batching/quantization profiles per workload. caching options (prefix/KV cash in the transcript) - sorry - KV cache, can significantly lower token costs for repeated contexts; the platform automatically supports prefix caching for common prompts. We'll share a doc with recommended settings.
21:41 - 24:10 Sofia Gomez: any gotchas with model parity between Hosted and Dedicated? we run some Mistral-like models. will performance change with quantization or diff hardware?

24:11 - 26:55 Daniel Park: core idea: model artifacts are the same; the runtime chooses optimized kernels based on hardware and sequence length. you may see differences in latency and cost due to quantization or different GPU types but results/outputs are functionally equivalent. we can pin model version to keep parity during rollouts.
26:56 - 29:30 Liam O'Connor: And SDKs - languages? node, python? any example infra templates or k8s helm charts for private?

29:31 - 31:50 Ava Martinez: We have official SDKs for python/node/go, plus quickstart templates and a sample k8s helm chart for private deploys. we'll attach links in the follow-up. rapid devs typically use our python SDK and hit first token in demo apps within minutes. also have a Postman collection.
31:51 - 35:15 Raj Patel: Pricing - how does hosted pricing compare to dedicated committed capacity? and how hard is it to switch?

35:16 - 38:00 Maya Singh: hosting is usage-based, good for experimentation. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit costs at commit volumes. Switching from Hosted to Dedicated is designed to be smooth - same API, you can pin model versions and route traffic. we'll provide a pricing estimate for your 100k tokens/day scenario.
38:01 - 41:25 Priya Rao: One more security detail - SSO (SAML/SCIM) support and role-based access? We need to restrict keys and team access in prod.

41:26 - 44:10 Daniel Park: yes SSO, SAML, SCIM and RBAC are supported on Dedicated/Private and can be added for Hosted enterprise customers. We'll include steps to enable SSO and options for key rotation and HSM-backed KMS in the security pack we'll share.
44:11 - 47:00 Raj Patel: Operationally, what's the SLA and outage fallbacks? if model endpoints go down how do you handle graceful degradation?

47:01 - 49:30 Maya Singh: We offer SLA options on Dedicated and Enterprise Hosted. runtime has smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants and region failover. for PLG quickstarts you get the hosted reliability tier; for production we recommend Dedicated with SLA and can set up canary rollouts.

49:31 - 51:10 Ava Martinez: Recap and next steps - we'll send: 1) PLG quickstart guide + free credits link, 2) SOC2/security whitepaper and KMS options, 3) benchmark template/plan for the 100k tokens/day sim, 4) pricing estimate. Let's tentatively schedule the technical deep dive for next Thursday at 10am PT. Any final questions?
51:11 - 52:00 Raj Patel: looks good. Sofia will coordinate schedules, Priya will share security constraints. thanks everyone.
Links and references: Quickstart guide: https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart | Security whitepaper: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf | Benchmark template (to be shared)
Notes: some words auto-transcribed (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache), minor speaker attribution errors possible.
